steps.thought: Question 1: how much of the platform exists? Measure, do not estimate: count Go/TS lines, tests, routes, and which spec pages are real vs placeholder.

Measured: 7,948 lines Go/SQL, 11,230 lines frontend, 57 Go tests, 18 routes, 32 API handlers. Built and verified against a real device: auth+roles, inventory CRUD+credentials, collection (version/time/status/optics/identity), ingest, logs. Fixture-backed or missing: incidents, reports, optical page, collection health, diagnostics console, settings writes, 2FA, lockout, multi-vendor adapters, thresholds by model.

Security: npm audit = 3 moderate, 0 high/critical (react-router open redirect + SSR hydration CVE, minimatch dev-only DoS). Go govulncheck = 52 reachable, but 36 are stdlib at go1.22.2 — the sandbox toolchain, fixed long before the Go 1.27 used in Termux. 12 are real modules: x/crypto 0.27 (10, incl. SSH DoS) and x/text 0.18 (2).

Verdict: GitHub cannot be read unauthenticated (401 on dependabot alerts), so the local audits are the evidence. None of the findings is critical for this deployment; the two real risks are both client-side-ish: an SSH DoS when dialling a hostile server, and an open redirect that needs an attacker-controlled link target we do not have. Fix by bumping x/crypto and x/text, and decide on react-router 7 separately.
